title: One game a week with AI, for a year. Game #1
author: Groowl
selftext:
I've set myself a challenge: one game a week for a year, built with Claude Code. Game #1 is out: Shuriken Slam Jam, a one-button roguelite where your shuriken bounces off the walls and the upgrades stack until one throw clears the screen.

One game a week is impossible if I write the code. It's possible if the AI writes it and I do the design. What actually makes the pace hold:

1. A CLAUDE.md with a "where to go" table (I want to change X → this file, this function), so every request starts in the right place instead of searching the whole codebase.
2. A balancing bot. The game runs headless, a bot plays real runs on the real code and tells me how far a build goes. I don't spend my week playtesting numbers.
3. A capture tool. It plays the game with chosen upgrades and records clips, so the GIFs and the trailer don't eat my week either.
4. No art files. Every sprite is drawn in code, the music is synthesized. Nothing to wait for.

What's still 100% my job: deciding what's fun. The AI never told me a boss was boring.

Game #1, free in your browser: https://groowl.itch.io/shuriken-slam-jam-demo

If you build with AI: what's the one tool or rule that doubled your speed?
